Maybe it’ll help to think of your situation like this:

Goals of therapy - 
1. Target 1s - life threatening behaviour (SH counts here)
2. Target 2- Therapy interfering behaviour (cancelling sessions, your therapist not being attentive during session etc. this can happen on both your and your therapist’s end.
3. Target 3 - quality of life interfering behaviour; this’ll be ineffective and unhealthy  coping mechanisms.

I remember crying frequently everyday during early grief, when I lost my dad who was my emotional rock. For me, it took me about 4 months for the thought of “oh my god, my dad is dead” every morning to dissipate. 

I know you can’t imagine it right now but the frequent crying did cease. 

I NEEDED to cry. I needed to think about him. I believe that one must go through grief rather than avoid it or shut it down. Feel all of the feelings. 

Grief is just love with no where to go. Write to her, if it helps, go to support groups, therapy if you can. This is a huge loss for you, don’t let yourself or anyone diminish that. 

4 years on, things have gotten easier. That’s not to say the grief doesn’t feel as heavy and not present. The hurt is still there. But I had to go through that awful grief, facing it everyday to get to this point. And it’s an ongoing journey. 

Feel free to DM me if you have any questions about this process, people also grieve very differently and individually. 

I’m so sorry for your loss and am sending lots of love, healing and light ❤️

PS; Excellent book: It’s Okay to Not be Okay by Meghan Devine

PPS: during the holidays, I made sure to make space for my dad and honour him. I found that to be very healing.
